text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.75% today to close at $413.92, continuing a sharp upward run that's seen the stock climb 8% over the past two weeks. The immediate catalyst appears to be oil price volatility and refining conditions: while crude fell slightly today after news that a damaged Saudi pipeline will restart soon, U.S. oil sits at $107 per barrel and refineries nationwide are running at 96.8% capacity — near their operational maximum. That combination of tight refinery operations and persistent fuel demand (diesel hit an all-time high of $6.31 per gallon this week) has been pushing refiner margins higher, which directly benefits Marathon's bottom line.

The broader backdrop is tightening global oil supply underpinned by geopolitical risk. A Houthi drone strike on Mecca and ongoing tensions around the Strait of Hormuz have kept crude elevated, while new reports of U.S. oil companies potentially developing Venezuelan reserves signal longer-term supply uncertainty. For a major refiner like Marathon, these conditions — scarce refined products, tight capacity, and elevated crude costs that it can pass through to customers — create a favorable margin environment that has driven the stock's two-week rally.
